chunks: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Aban, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: Ten men killed one man.

He عليه السلام said: If his heirs wish, they may kill them all together and pay nine blood monies. And if they wish to choose one man and kill him, they may kill him, and the remaining nine shall pay to the family of the slain last one one-tenth of the blood money, each man among them.
He عليه السلام said: Then indeed the governor undertakes their discipline and imprisonment.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the family or entitled heirs of the person who was killed
key_terms.أَوْلِيَاؤُهُ: the heirs or legal claimants of the murdered person who hold the right of retaliation
key_terms.الْوَالِيَ: the governing authority responsible for enforcing punishment and public order
key_terms.دِيَاتٍ: blood monies paid as financial compensation for unlawful killing
key_terms.عُشْرَ الدِّيَةِ: one-tenth of the blood money owed by each of the remaining killers in this case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a group of people jointly kill one man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a case in which a group jointly kills one person. It explains the options of the victim's heirs regarding retaliation and blood money, and it also assigns the ruler a role in disciplining and imprisoning the offenders.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5230 - Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated from Aban from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasar, who said:
I asked Abu Jafar (as) about ten men who killed a man.

Imam (as) said: "If the heirs of the murdered person wish, they may kill all of them and pay nine blood monies (diyyat). But if they prefer to choose one of them to execute, they may do so, and the remaining nine must each pay one-tenth of the blood money to the heirs of the murdered person."
Imam (as) added, "Afterward, the governor is responsible for disciplining and imprisoning them."
